messages:
mel: heads-up — since ~00:15 we lost ~12% GPU capacity in us-west2. Node telemetry shows a spike in correctable ECC and repeated PCIe retrain events after last-night's DDR microcode refresh. batch jobs started failing with OOMs and soft-restarts.

owen: can you paste the brief logs/metric slices? which racks/nodes are noisy?

mel: quick sample from host rack-17-05 kernel: 
```
[00:16:12] kernel: nvlink: link retrain timeout on GPU 0
[00:16:13] kernel: nvidia: GPU 0: ECC_CORRECTABLE_COUNT increased by 42
[00:16:18] kernel: nvidia: SM reset sequence initiated
[00:16:20] kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=0005
```
hosts: rack-17-{01..12} and rack-21-03 showing >30% of the events.

owen: ok. not seeing the typical Xid-31 storm, more like persistent mem-correctables + link retrains. might be microcode/DDR timing regression. starting targeted probes.

k8s-bot: pods on node rack-17-05 are being evicted due to NodePressure:memory (evicted 12 pods).

jia: can we soft-drain noisy hosts and leave the rest? prefer avoid full rack drains if we can isolate cards.

mel: plan suggestion: 1) run probe on affected hosts to confirm per-GPU ECC trend 2) soft-drain worst nodes (one rack at a time) 3) route latency-sensitive traffic to dedicated pool/us-west1 fallback 4) open vendor escalation for microcode rollback/analysis.

sam: routing to dedicated pool will spike costs — rough estimate +$8k/day if full spillover. we should be conservative with spillover and prefer staged drains first. :money_with_wings:

owen: running probe now: `sudo /opt/infra/tools/probe_gpu_health --hosts rack-17-0{1..12} --metrics ecc,link,sm_reset --output short`

mel: probe output snippet: 
```
rack-17-05.gpu0 ECC: 128/min link_retrain: 23 SM_resets: 4
rack-17-06.gpu1 ECC: 110/min link_retrain: 19 SM_resets: 3
rack-21-03.gpu2 ECC: 95/min link_retrain: 12 SM_resets: 2
```

infra-oncall: i started soft-drain on rack-17-05 (cordon + evict non-critical pods). will monitor latency.

jia: please prioritize keeping capacity for SLO-critical routes. we can redirect batch jobs to a paused queue.

vendor-ops-bot: vendor update: "We observed similar symptoms after the DDR microcode refresh in a small customer cohort. Suggested next steps: collect full nv-hostdump, kernel dmesg, motherboard BIOS revision, and schedule microcode rollback if pattern confirmed. Potential RMA on 6 GPUs if errors persist post-rollback."

mel: collecting hostdumps now and will upload to the vendor ticket. proposing: 1 rack soft-drain, wait 30m; if noise drops, continue staged; if not, schedule maintenance window for rollback.

sam: +1 to staged drains. reopen if we need to shift traffic to reserved capacity. finance aware of potential short-term spike.

own: rolling update note: avoid rebooting entire rack at once — reboot per host after cordon to reduce job churn. I'll script the sequence.

mel: thanks — will keep thread updated. tagging @infra-oncall for visibility. :eyes:
